title: Hamilton set for further grid penalty in Sao Paulo
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton is set to start the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from the back of the grid as the Ferrari driver is prepared to take a further penalty.

The seven-time World Champion was set to receive a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday's race at the Autódromo José Carlos Pace along with team mate Charles Leclerc, as both drivers had a change of Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) on their cars.

But during Free Practice 3 on Saturday, Hamilton reported vibrations on his engine and returned to the pit lane for checks.

Rejoining the circuit in the final hour of practice, Hamilton immediately suffered a loss of power followed by smoke in the cockpit, eventually returning to the garage and ending his session as Ferrari investigated.

Ahead of Qualifying later on Saturday, Ferrari confirmed that Hamilton would take part in the session but that the entire power unit had been replaced.

"Following today’s FP3 session, the power unit fitted to car #44 was removed for further checks," read a team statement.

"After completing our analysis, we have decided to replace the entire power unit. Lewis will take part in Qualifying but will have to start tomorrow’s race from the back of the grid."

It means Hamilton will start at the back, where he will be joined by Max Verstappen as the Red Bull driver also had various elements of his power unit changed ahead of FP3.

title: Verstappen beats Antonelli and Norris in Sao Paulo FP3
excerpt:
Max Verstappen finished fastest in Free Practice 3 ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, the Red Bull driver beating Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris to the top of the leaderboard.

The Dutchman, who is due to serve a grid penalty for Sunday's race, posted a 1m 11.622s, leaving him just 0.025s clear of Antonelli at the Autódromo José Carlos Pace, the venue confirmed as staying on the Formula 1 calendar until 2035.

Despite the threat of rain and thunderstorms in the area, most drivers and teams were in no rush to immediately head out once the session began at 1130 local time on Saturday.

One driver to venture out was Nico Hulkenberg, the Audi driver having had no running on Friday as his car was driven by Freddie Slater in FP1, before the rookie suffered an early mechanical issue which curtailed any further running.

George Russell was another to hit the track, the Briton set for a five-place grid penalty due to an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) change, while Mercedes team mate Antonelli reported a problem with his steering wheel.

The potential issue didn't prevent the new World Champion from jumping to the top of the times at the 10-minute mark, the Italian posting a 1m 12.497s as all drivers used Pirelli's medium tyre for their runs.

Lance Stroll's challenging season continued as the Aston Martin driver was soon told of a problem with his car and to return to the pits, the Canadian's running coming to an end after just 15 minutes due to an Energy Recover System (ERS) issue.

Antonelli lowered the benchmark further, posting a 1m 12.214s to go fractionally faster than Verstappen, with the Dutchman running off the track at Turn 4 when attempting to respond with another effort.

The Red Bull driver is set to start from the back of the grid in Brazil after several power unit changes, with both Ferrari's of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc also given 10-place grid drops for ICE changes.

Hamilton could be due further power unit changes, though, the Briton reporting of "strange vibrations with the engine" and returning to the pits.

The seven-time World Champion eventually headed back out but returned immediately with "smoke in the cockpit" and a sub-optimal engine noise, with his session coming to an end as 25 minutes remained on the clock.

It took until just 15 minutes remained for drivers and teams to finally focus on Qualifying simulations, with the Pirelli soft tyre making an appearance for the first time in FP3.

Russell became the first driver to dip below the 1m 12s barrier, but he was quickly usurped by Norris, Antonelli and finally Verstappen, the latter sitting fastest on a 1m 11.622s as the quartet were covered by less than two tenths.

Attempts to improve on a second lap with the same set of tyres generally failed throughout the field, leaving Verstappen fastest at the chequered flag from Antonelli, Norris and Russell, just as heavy rain arrived.

Leclerc, Oscar Piastri (McLaren), the Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson, Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto completed the top 10.

Pierre Gasly's Alpine was P11 from Hamilton, Hulkenberg, Franco Colapinto (Alpine), and Haas drivers Rafael Camara and Ollie Bearman.

The order was completed by Alex Albon (Williams), Fernando Alonso's Aston Martin, Carlos Sainz (Williams), Sergio Perez, the Cadillac driver placed under investgiation for discarding something from his cockpit, team mate Valtteri Bottas and Stroll.

title: Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen take Brazil grid drops
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen will take grid drops at this weekend’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix after Ferrari and Red Bull changed power unit components within their cars.

Ferrari have exceeded the season allowance for the Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) on both Hamilton and Leclerc’s cars, earning 10-place drops. However, Hamilton is now set for an additional penalty that will see him start from the back of the grid after the Scuderia were forced to change the whole power unit, with the new engine suffering problems in FP3.

Red Bull, meanwhile, have gone over the limit for the ICE, Turbo Charger and Exhaust on Verstappen’s car, earning him a back-of-the-grid start after he amassed 30 places worth of penalties.

In another change, 2026 newcomers Cadillac have given Sergio Perez a new Ferrari ICE, Turbo Charger and Motor Generator Unit-Kinetic (MGU-K), which also leads to a back-of-the-grid start for the Mexican.

As per the regulations, the first time the allocation of any one of the elements is exceeded, a 10-place grid penalty is applied, with the second time this occurs (and so on) resulting in a five-place grid drop – all penalties at the same event applying in a cumulative manner.

If a driver incurs a penalty exceeding 15 grid places, they will be required to start the race at the back of the field regardless.

Hamilton, Verstappen and Leclerc are therefore set to tumble down the order from wherever they qualify on Saturday, setting up recovery drives in Sunday’s Grand Prix.

Hamilton famously recovered from the back of the grid across the Sprint and Grand Prix in Sao Paulo back in 2021 – having been disqualified from Friday Qualifying for a Drag Reduction System irregularity, and a subsequent five-place grid penalty for an engine change.

Verstappen also delivered comebacks in 2024 (when he started 17th after a dramatic Qualifying session and an engine penalty, and rose to victory) and 2025 (when Red Bull made various changes to his car after another tough Qualifying, meaning he started from the pit lane, before climbing to third).

Mercedes driver George Russell had already confirmed that he will be taking a five-place grid penalty this weekend for a similar engine change.

title: F1 to race in Sao Paulo through to 2035 following new deal
excerpt:
Formula 1 will continue to race in Brazil through to 2035 following a five-year extension, securing the future of one of the sport’s most iconic and historic venues.

The Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace – otherwise known as Interlagos – has been part of the calendar for over 50 years and delivered plenty of memorable races, such as Max Verstappen’s 2024 charge from P17 to victory.

Combining an undulating layout with Brazil’s passion for motorsport, the track consistently produces exciting wheel-to-wheel racing in front of vibrant crowds, and has seen a total of six Drivers’ Championships be decided, including those won by current drivers Fernando Alonso and Lewis Hamilton.

The country’s fanbase has increased to 75.8 million – 44% of whom are female and 41% of whom are under 35 – whilst attendances at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix have also grown, reaching 303,627 in 2025, up from 291,717 the year before.

Furthermore, F1 delivers a significant economic impact in the local community and more widely, with the 2025 event providing R$2.3 billion for Sao Paulo – a 9.7% increase compared to the previous record in 2024.

The sport also entered into an agreement last year with Brazilian broadcaster Globo, giving paying subscribers to SporTV the option to watch every on-track session live and on-demand, with additional live free-to-air coverage of 15 Grands Prix available throughout the season.

As part of the new five-year extension, the office of the Mayor of Sao Paulo, Ricardo Nunes, will continue to make significant investments to deliver a world-class spectacle, further enhancing the experience for fans and guests in the years ahead.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, said: “Brazil is an important part of Formula 1’s history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035.

“The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo.

Everything you need to know about the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace

“Brazil has produced an incredible 33 Formula 1 drivers, including Gabriel Bortoleto and Rafael Camara who are racing this weekend in front of their home crowd, which will add to the many previous unforgettable racing moments in Sao Paulo.

“The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil.

“I would like to thank the Mayor of Sao Paulo, Nunes, and the President and CEO of Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Alan Adler, for their continued commitment and investment. Together, we will build on this success and make the experience even better for our fans in the years ahead.”

Nunes, Mayor of Sao Paulo, said: “The renewal of the Formula 1 contract for a further five years is a very significant achievement for Sao Paulo.

“We are ensuring the continuity of one of the world’s biggest sporting events, which boosts the economy, creates jobs, strengthens tourism and raises our city’s international profile.

“Formula 1 benefits a wide range of sectors, such as hotels, restaurants, retail and services, generating opportunities and income for the local population.

“Sao Paulo has a long-standing tradition and a historic relationship with Formula 1. Maintaining this partnership means ensuring predictability for investment, strengthening the calendar of major events and consolidating the city’s position as a global benchmark for hosting international competitions.”

Adler, CEO of Sao Paulo Grand Prix, said: “The extension of the contract of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix until 2035 is a source of immense pride, and represents recognition of work built on dedication, investment and a long-term vision.

“This renewal reaffirms Sao Paulo’s place amongst the world’s leading motorsport destinations.

“Interlagos is a unique circuit, admired by drivers, teams and fans from all over the world. It has been the setting for memorable races and is an integral part of Formula 1’s history.

“I would like to thank Domenicali and Formula 1 for their trust and partnership, as well as Mayor Nunes and Sao Paulo City Council for their extraordinary support and ongoing investment in the modernisation of Interlagos. This partnership has been fundamental to the growth and success of the event.”

title: Permane gives update on Racing Bulls driver decision process
excerpt:
Alan Permane believes that "the right decision will be made" when Racing Bulls finally confirms its 2027 driver line-up, with the team "trying to apply a little bit of science" before making any announcement.

Racing Bulls remains the only team yet to announce even one driver for next season, with both seats up for grabs and three drivers fighting for them.

Current driver Liam Lawson sits best of the rest in the drivers' standings behind the top teams, with the Kiwi sitting in P9 having also made three appearances for Red Bull this season, scoring 14 times on a Sunday.

Arvid Lindblad sits P11 in the standings, albeit 45 points behind Lawson, but has impressed in a rookie Formula 1 season that has included 11 points finishes in Grands Prix.

Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov is the third driver in contention, the Bulgarian a race winner in F2 and second in the standings during his maiden season in the junior single-seater series.

Having made his F1 debut during Free Practice 1 in Mexico, Tsolov was directly compared against Lindblad during the session, finishing just one-tenth slower.

Speaking to the media on Friday ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix this weekend, Permane stated that the team were in no rush to confirm a line-up.

"Red Bull has had a very successful young driver programme," said Permane, who announced he had signed a contract extension to stay with Racing Bulls until 2031.

"And I think, and I don't want to be critical of it, but I think you guys are critical of it, [that] maybe sometimes drivers haven't been able to have enough time to settle or maybe some snap decisions have been made.

"We're trying to apply a little bit of science and that takes some time. We are looking at everything and studying, analysing and time is on our side.

"We're not in a rush to do anything and I'm very confident the right decision will be made. I realise it's frustrating for our drivers, I realise it's frustrating for everyone else, but we want to get it right and we will get it right, and I'm sure when we announce it in the coming weeks everyone will be happy."

Ahead of this weekend's race in Brazil, Lawson admitted "I don’t know what else they want me to do" having first made his F1 debut in 2023, but only completing a full campaign last season for the first time.

Permane admitted that the main area of focus would be the outright speed of a driver, but that attributes such as experience would also be an important factor in any decision.

"Main factors are, as always, pace and speed. That's what comes into it. That's the very first thing we look for but we're not just a team that exists to just solely compete," said Permane.

"We are here to bring young talent through so we have to keep an eye on that and that doesn't necessarily mean that we just keep churning young talent through the car.

"We need to have maybe some experience as well to measure that talent against. So it's not an easy decision and I understand, I get the frustration from everyone.

"I get the frustration from my drivers, however, they are both performing excellently and so I don't know if that frustration is helping, maybe they'll be even better when those decisions are made."

title: Red Bull branded ‘pathetic’ if Max Verstappen clash triggers Liam Lawson exit
excerpt:
Martin Brundle has branded Red Bull "pathetic" if the Mexico City Grand Prix practice clash between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen plays any part in the New Zealander losing his Racing Bulls seat for 2027.

Lawson and Verstappen collided during FP2 in Mexico, with both drivers compensating for lost track time after handing their cars to rookies Ayumu Iwasa and Nikola Tsolov in the opening session.

FIA stewards handed each driver a one-place grid penalty and a penalty point on their superlicence, judging the pair equally at fault.

Lawson's 2027 future remains unresolved, with Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane confirming the squad is weighing up Lawson against junior prospects Arvid Lindblad and Tsolov for its two race seats.

Tsolov, who deputised for Lawson in FP1 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, is understood to be the frontrunner reported to replace him should the 24-year-old be dropped.

Speaking to Sky F1, Brundle said any link between the incident and Lawson's contract situation would reflect badly on Red Bull.

"If he dared be on the racetrack on a preparation lap like Max at the same moment, if that's a factor in him getting the heave-ho, that's pathetic," said Brundle.

"That's so childish. I can't believe it is. I think that's just an excuse if they are using that.

"So either he's got a brilliant poker face, or he knows he's out of there, which is quite something."

Martin Brundle personal experience shows strong results not always enough

Brundle knows from personal experience that such decisions are not always made purely on merit.

He was dropped by Benetton at the end of 1992 in favour of Riccardo Patrese despite having often matched Michael Schumacher's pace that season.

"I remember starting to beat Michael Schumacher in the Benetton team and I got biffed at the end of the year," added Brundle.

"It happens in this business for any number of reasons, sometimes commercial reasons, political, future, and the teams are thinking a long way ahead.

"All the pieces of the jigsaw fit together in a way that doesn't always look obvious to us standing here talking about it right now.

"But I think Liam's done a tremendous job for them."

title: Torrential downpour sparks early Sao Paulo GP qualifying red flag
excerpt:
FIA race director Rui Marques was forced to red-flag the São Paulo Grand Prix qualifying inside three minutes after the heavens opened over Interlagos.

The majority of the drivers were ready on intermediate tyres in the pit lane as they waited for qualifying to start. That followed a thunderstorm that hit the circuit not long after the final practice session had concluded, leaving the track wet.

But as the clock ticked towards the start of qualifying, a torrential downpour swept over the track.

Several drivers managed to take on the extreme-wet compound for the out lap, but the rain rapidly grew in intensity.

After two minutes and 23 seconds of qualifying, Marques called a halt.

The FIA announced at 15:09 local time, nine minutes after qualifying had started, that it expected the level of rain "to continue for about 10 minutes".

A spokesperson added: "Once the conditions improve, we intend to send the medical car on track to assess the level of standing water."

After a tour of the circuit by the medical car, a further announcement from the FIA read: "Marshals currently working at various corners around the track to clear any standing water.

"The current low-level intensity of rain is expected to continue for the foreseeable future."

The safety car then ventured out for a couple of exploratory laps, just as the rain started to fall again.

A further FIA message, referring to safety car driver Bernd Maylander, read: "Bernd's feedback is that Turns 2, 3, and the areas from Turn 4 to 5 are the current issues where standing water could cause aquaplaning."

Following a second outing from Maylander, 45 minutes after qualifying was red-flagged, the FIA reported that "the feedback is not positive. Conditions have worsened since his last outing."

A third inspection occurred at ten past the hour, after which the FIA said: "Feedback is positive. Race control are hoping we'll be able to get this session restarted."

After an 82-minute delay, qualifying was finally given the green light to restart.

title: Lewis Hamilton handed further power unit punishment ahead of Sao Paulo GP
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has suffered a further blow to his São Paulo Grand Prix hopes after being hit with a second power unit penalty.

Hamilton went into the final practice session at Interlagos with a new internal combustion engine in his SF-26, earning a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday's race. The Scuderia also handed team-mate Charles Leclerc a new ICE.

Thirty-five minutes into the session, however, Hamilton announced over the radio that he had "smoke in the cockpit" of his car, and that he was heading back to the pits.

On pulling into his pit box, plumes of smoke emerged from various areas of the car. Hamilton did not take any further part in FP3.

On further investigation, Ferrari has decided to make further PU changes, which means the seven-time F1 champion will now join Red Bull's Max Verstappen at the back of the grid.

A Ferrari spokesperson said: "Following today’s FP3 session, the power unit fitted to car #44 was removed for further checks.

"After completing our analysis, we have decided to replace the entire power unit. Lewis will take part in qualifying but will have to start tomorrow’s race from the back of the grid.

title: Sergio Perez handed 'not appropriate' verdict by Sao Paulo stewards over cable tie
excerpt:
Sergio Perez has been handed a formal warning by the São Paulo Grand Prix stewards after throwing a cable organiser out of the cockpit of his Cadillac during final practice.

Late in the hour-long session at Interlagos, the stewards cited Perez for 'alleged driving in an unsafe condition' after reviewing in-car footage of the Mexican's act.

Over the radio, Perez was asked by his race engineer, Carlo Pasetti: "We saw you throwing something out of your car on the outlap. What was it?"

Perez replied: "I don't know. It was, errr, something came off. I think the radio, where you put the radio cables. A little box."

Pasetti replied: "Copy that. We will investigate."

The stewards also investigated, with a document reading: "The stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed in-car video evidence and determined that the driver of car 11 threw a small plastic piece out of the car.

"The plastic piece was a cable organiser that typically attaches to the seat belt. It dislodged during the session, and the driver threw it out as he was concerned that it would lodge itself somewhere else in the car and create a safety issue.

"While we appreciated the fact that it was a small, light piece of plastic that was unlikely to cause any damage to another car or injure another driver, throwing materials onto the track during a live session is not appropriate for obvious reasons."

title: Breaking: Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen grid penalties confirmed
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen both know exactly how to bounce back from São Paulo grid penalties!

The FIA has confirmed that Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen will all serve a grid penalty in the São Paulo Grand Prix.

Hamilton and Leclerc both endured a difficult opening day in Interlagos with the Scuderia once again struggling at high-speed, with the decision being taken to fit a new engine outside their allocated pools.

The seven-time world champion and Leclerc have both received a 10-place grid penalty after taking a new internal combustion engine, the first of that component outside their legal pools.

Friday was also challenging for Verstappen, with Red Bull deciding to perform several power unit component changes. As a result, the Dutchman will likely start from the last row of the grid.

Verstappen has taken a new internal combustion engine, turbocharger and exhaust set, resulting in a 30-place grid penalty. Each component is the first outside the allocated pool.

Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen are not the only drivers affected this weekend.

George Russell will also drop five places after Mercedes fitted an additional internal combustion engine outside his allocation, following a mechanical failure that forced the team into a larger power unit change at the Singapore Grand Prix earlier in the season.

Cadillac's Sergio Perez has also received a 30-place grid penalty after taking a new internal combustion engine, turbocharger and MGU-K.

Lewis Hamilton needing 2021 repeat; Max Verstappen 2024 wet masterclass

It would not be the first time Hamilton or Verstappen has turned a grid penalty at this circuit into a triumph.

Back in 2021, when he was still driving for Mercedes, Hamilton was handed a five-place grid drop in Brazil after the team installed a fifth internal combustion engine of that season, exceeding his allocation.

Mercedes had made the change due to concerns over power degradation and reliability issues linked to earlier power unit batches.

Hamilton was further demoted to the back of the Sprint grid that weekend after being disqualified from qualifying, with stewards ruling that the gap between his rear wing's DRS elements had exceeded the permitted 85-millimetre limit, a defect attributed to mechanical damage rather than deliberate rule-breaking.

Despite starting that race down in tenth, Hamilton produced a dominant drive through the field at Interlagos to take victory ahead of Max Verstappen, underlining just how much overtaking opportunity the circuit can offer even from a compromised grid slot.

Verstappen produced one of the great recovery drives of his career at the venue in 2024, storming from 17th on the grid in treacherous, rain-affected conditions to win going away, setting the fastest lap along the way as he beat Esteban Ocon by nearly 20 seconds.

Pierre Gasly completed an Alpine one-two in third, while Hamilton could only salvage 10th from 14th on the grid that day.

title: Legendary fan favourite F1 grand prix handed contract extension
excerpt:
The São Paulo Grand Prix has had its contract extended until the 2035 season, Formula 1 has officially confirmed.

Interlagos is one of the most popular stops on the calendar among fans and drivers. The circuit near São Paulo has a long history of producing drama, helped in no small part by its famously unpredictable weather.

Over the years it has hosted numerous iconic races, including several memorable wet-weather drives.

Max Verstappen famously rose from starting at the back of the grid to win in treacherous conditions in 2023, while Lewis Hamilton won from 10th in 2021.

The 2008 edition also remains etched in the sport's history, when Lewis Hamilton passed Timo Glock through the final corner complex on the last lap to seal his maiden world title.

Interlagos was already contracted to host the race through to 2030. Formula 1 has now extended that deal further, meaning the São Paulo is set to remain on the calendar for five more years beyond that date.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of F1, said: "Brazil is an important part of Formula 1’s history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in São Paulo until 2035.

"The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of São Paulo. Brazil has produced an incredible 33 Formula 1 drivers, including Gabriel Bortoleto and Rafael Câmara who are racing this weekend in front of their home crowd, which will add to the many previous unforgettable racing moments in São Paulo.

"The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil. I would like to thank the Mayor of São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes, and the President and CEO of São Paulo Grand Prix, Alan Adler, for their continued commitment and investment.

"Together, we will build on this success and make the experience even better for our fans in the years ahead."

title: Max Verstappen responds to major grid penalty for the São Paulo GP
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has confirmed he will start Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix from the back of the grid due to a power unit change.

The announcement came on Saturday afternoon, with the Milton Keynes-based squad opting to fit the fresh PU after the four-time F1 champion struggled with engine braking and clutch issues during Friday's running at Interlagos.

The timing of the change means qualifying has effectively lost its relevance for the Dutchman this weekend, with Verstappen already guaranteed to line up last regardless of how he performs.

Speaking to Viaplay, Verstappen explained the thinking behind the decision.

"Qualifying doesn't really matter that much, to be honest," Verstappen said, laughing. "I'm starting last anyway, because we have a new engine in the car.

"It makes sense that you'd go all out right away. That decision was made sometime after Friday's session, because we saw that it needed to be replaced."

The 29-year-old is no stranger to recovery drives from the back of the field at Interlagos, having done so before, but he made clear the novelty has worn off.

"At some point, you just get tired of it, right? Sure, it was fun, but I don't really want to do it here every year," he said. "But yeah, that's just how it is."

As for Saturday's running, Verstappen shrugged off its significance entirely.

"That's why today doesn't really matter all that much," he added. "It's just going to be a bit of a long day..."

title: Mercedes facing unexpected problem after powerful Sao Paulo GP start
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli made a perfect start to life as world champion in Interlagos by topping FP2.

Mercedes has admitted both George Russell and Kimi Antonelli are battling understeer for the first time since the team's major upgrade package landed in Malaysia, despite Antonelli topping Friday's second practice session at Interlagos.

The Italian set the pace with a 1:10.763, edging out Lando Norris and Max Verstappen, with Russell fourth fastest as Mercedes continued to look competitive on Friday.

But Mercedes' deputy team principal Bradley Lord struck a cautious tone when discussing the car's underlying balance, pointing to a handling trait the squad had not seen since introducing its seven-part aerodynamic update at Sepang.

Speaking after FP2, Lord said the Silver Arrows look in the fight but that understeer needs dialling out for both drivers.

"Real progress is hitting the ground running with the car," said Lord. "Both drivers are still looking to dial out some understeer, which is not something we've had too much of since we put the update package on in Malaysia.

"So, overall, long-run pace looks in the mix with Lando [Norris], Max [Verstappen] and both of our guys. So maybe Ferrari are half a step behind, but I'm sure they'll come good as well in the hotter conditions."

Has Mercedes finally understood Malaysia upgrades?

Conditions at Interlagos on Friday turned changeable, with air temperatures dropping below 20 degrees Celsius during FP2 and light drizzle disrupting tyre warm-up.

Saturday is forecast to be considerably warmer, before temperatures fall again on race day, a swing Lord suggested would offer a genuine test of how well Mercedes understands its new aerodynamic package across varying track conditions.

Asked whether the operating window of the upgrade is becoming better understood within the team, Lord was candid about the uncertainty that remains.

"That's a good question," said Lord. "I'm not quite sure how we would answer that, to be honest. We'll see.

"This weekend we've got a great test of it, with cool conditions [on Friday], much warmer on Saturday and then cool again on Sunday, and whether we can cope with that sort of adjustment in track temperature and what it does to the balance as well."

title: Max Verstappen set for major back of the grid Sao Paulo GP penalty
excerpt:
Max Verstappen is set to start Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix from the back of the grid after Red Bull opted to fit a fresh power unit to his car, according to reports.

According to De Telegraaf, Red Bull had planned to delay a scheduled engine change for as long as possible this season, but problems emerged with the power unit on Friday at Interlagos.

The team has decided the risk of continuing without a swap was too great, prompting the full change of engine that now triggers the grid drop.

Verstappen is no stranger to fighting back from the rear of the field at Interlagos. Last year he started from the pit lane following an engine change and still came home third.

In 2024, in wet conditions, the four-time champion started 17th and produced a dominant drive to win the race outright.

The four-time world champion is not alone in having a grid penalty for what is expected to be a wet race on Sunday, with George Russell and Lewis Hamilton also facing demotions.

title: Lewis Hamilton set for Sao Paulo GP grid penalty after difficult start
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton is set to take a grid penalty at Interlagos this weekend after Ferrari opted for a fresh engine element beyond his season allocation, RacingNews365 understands.

Under FIA sporting regulations, exceeding the permitted number of power unit components triggers a 10-place grid penalty for the first additional element introduced, dropping to five places for any further changes beyond that point.

It remains unclear exactly where Hamilton will be demoted to on the grid once qualifying is completed and whether it is a full engine change.

The timing is notable given the parallel with 2021, when Hamilton took a five-place penalty for fitting a fifth Mercedes engine of that season ahead of the same event.

Starting 10th that day, Hamilton produced one of the defining drives of his career, working through a two-stop strategy on medium and then hard tyres to hunt down and pass Max Verstappen for the win.

Interlagos lends itself to recovery drives of that nature. The long uphill run from Junção through Arquibancadas feeds a slipstreaming blast into the Senna S, setting up a counter-attack opportunity moments later into Turn 4.

The compact 4.309km lap keeps the field tightly bunched across all 71 laps, while heavy tyre degradation through the circuit's high-load corners regularly produces pace deltas that reward cars running fresher rubber.

Changeable weather at the São Paulo venue has historically added another layer of unpredictability, increasing both driver error and the scope for late-race passing moves.

Hamilton arrives at the circuit third in the drivers' championship on 259 points, just two behind Verstappen, with Ferrari needing a repeat of that 2021 charge.
